🏛️ Ethics & Safety

EU AI Act

In simple words

The European Union's law on artificial intelligence, adopted in 2024 and often called the world's first broad AI law.

The European Union's law on artificial intelligence, adopted in 2024 and often described as the world's first broad AI law. It sorts AI systems by risk: a few uses are banned, high-risk uses (for example in hiring, schools or medicine) must follow strict rules, and people must be told when they are talking to an AI or looking at AI-made media. Its rules start to apply step by step, over several years.

Example. Under the law, a system that gives people scores for their social behaviour to decide how they are treated is banned, and a chatbot on a shop's website must make clear that you aren't talking to a person.

Related words

  • BiasWhen an AI system treats some people or groups unfairly, often because of unbalanced training data.
  • AI watermarkA hidden or visible mark added to AI-made pictures, audio, video or text to show that AI created them.
  • DeepfakeA fake video, image or voice recording made with AI that shows someone saying or doing something they never did.
